content.thinking:
I'm planning a treasure-hoard prop with a League of Legends aesthetic: glowing gems, an open chest with a radiant interior, a crown, goblets, and a mound of golden coins, keeping the whole footprint around 1.2 meters. Now I'm starting to build this out using the builder API.

For performance, I'm merging many small coin geometries (cylinders rotated and translated into a scattered pile) into a single part per color using BufferGeometryUtils, rather than creating hundreds of individual parts, and writing a helper function to accumulate transformed geometries before merging and adding them to the scene.

I'm designing the mound shape mathematically with a height falloff function so coins can be placed realistically on its surface with randomized tilt, and planning the treasure chest layout at the back of the scene—using a wood-grained box body with gold bands, and considering a lathed or extruded arched profile for an open lid rotated backward.

Working out the outline orientation vectors so the lid's bulge faces outward when rotated open, making sure the arch direction flips to point backward instead of toward the interior once the lid is standing upright.

Adding thin gold band extrusions offset along the lid's thickness direction, then building the chest body as a box positioned behind the lid, plus a glowing gold interior plane and a mound of coins for the treasure look.

For the gems, I'm scattering glowing octahedron and icosahedron shapes in hextech colors—cyan, magenta, emerald, ruby, violet—with some elongated and clustered into crystal formations, merging meshes by color for efficiency.

For the crown, I'm building a lathe-based hollow ring band with five spiked points topped with gems, positioning it tilted on the coin mound near the front right.

Shaping the goblet lathe profile...

I'm positioning goblets on the ground plane and planning coin stacks near the front—merging stacked and loose coin cylinders, with a lighter inner disc on top of each for a simple embossed-face effect, keeping triangle counts low.

Scaling coins down to 8-sided cylinders keeps the triangle budget manageable even with hundreds of coins and their inner discs. For the treasure chest, I'm planning wood-grain paint on the body, gold corner trims and lock plate with a glowing gem, plus vertical gold metal bands across the front.

I'm settling on a deep purple-violet wood with gold trim and cyan/magenta glow accents, positioning the front bands precisely relative to the box depth, and filling the interior with a glowing heap of coins represented as a flattened scaled sphere.

For background elements, I'm skipping light beam/aura effects since translucency isn't available, and instead planning a cluster of six-sided crystal spikes behind the chest at varying heights and a tilt-back position for depth, while deciding against adding extras like a scepter or sword.

Shaping a coin sack...

Confirming no edge crossing in the sack profile, then adding a tan rope tie and mottled brown sack texture. I'm setting up a scatter helper for placing coins randomly and a mound-height function to shape the coin pile, while checking the mound center doesn't overlap the chest's back edge.

Repositioning the mound to center around (0, 0, 0.2) with radius 0.6 so it overlaps the chest front naturally, like the pile is leaning against it. For the crown resting on top of the mound, I'm computing its sunk-in height based on the mound profile at its offset location, accepting that coins will partially cover it.

For the loose coins, I'm scattering 230 of them across the mound using random polar coordinates with height following the mound surface plus a small offset, random tilts and spin, while skipping zones too close to the crown, goblet, or chest body so they don't clip through those objects. I'm also adding 25 flat coins on the floor in a ring just outside the mound, avoiding the chest and sack areas.

Then I'm placing distinct coin stacks near the front of the mound at specific positions with varying heights (8, 5, 3 coins), stacking each coin with slight jitter and spacing based on coin thickness, making sure these stacks sit on the floor beyond the mound's extent.

Now I'm scattering roughly 28 gems across the mound, each randomly colored, shaped as icosahedrons or stretched octahedrons for a cut-gem look, sized small and rotated randomly, plus adding a few larger feature crystals like a big cyan hexagonal gem, with everything grouped by color and merged into efficient geometry collections.

I'm assigning gold tones to the coin groups and setting up a transform helper that composes position, rotation, and scale into a matrix to clone and reposition each gem geometry before merging.

For the crown itself, I'm planning a lathed band with gold cel-shaded paint, and alternating tall and short spikes placed around the ring at regular angles using a spike-generating helper with four-sided tips.

Pearls will sit on spike tips as small glowing spheres in a soft white-pink, with gemstones studded around the band for color accents. Inside, I'm lathing a crimson velvet dome that rises visibly above the band, defining its profile points to curve inward toward the top, then starting work on the band's own outline profile.

Adding decorative gold rings around the band and roughing out minor chest details like corner brackets and a small stack of gold bars for visual richness.

Still defining geometry params...

I'll scatter the coins slightly above the mound surface so they sit visibly on top, and position the mound within the chest so it overlaps naturally with the interior glow. Then I'll finalize and return the constructed scene root.
